claim.why_it_matters: Printed as a numbered section heading (sibling of '### 4.3.8.1 Qualification' on page 164); the markdown has it as a plain paragraph with no heading marker. A heading missing or at the wrong level breaks the section structure that navigation and clause lookup by section number rely on; the wording itself is intact.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page 167 (folio IV-21) prints '4.3.8.2 Subscripting' as a numbered section heading at the top of the page. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md (line 7006) it is a plain paragraph, while its sibling '4.3.8.1 Qualification' is '### 4.3.8.1 Qualification' (line 6892) and the following sibling is '#### 4.3.8.3 Function-Identifier' (line 7072). The wording is intact; only the heading marker is missing. The same page's sub-headings 4.3.8.2.1 Function, 4.3.8.2.2 General Format, 4.3.8.2.3 Syntax Rules and 4.3.8.2.4 General Rules are also plain paragraphs (lines 7008, 7012, 7028, 7054), unlike 4.3.8.3.x, which are '#####' headings. The running header 'Subscripting' at line 3 is page furniture and plays no part in this.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate as stated. In addition, the four sub-headings 4.3.8.2.1 to 4.3.8.2.4 on the same page are also plain paragraphs and lack heading markers. The heading levels for this subtree are also inconsistent with the surrounding text: 4.3.8.1 is ###, while 4.3.8.3 and 4.3.8.4 are ####.
